title: Second-vendor configuration envelope: clang-18 vs gcc-13, artifact level

scopeStatement.measures: Whether a security-relevant source construct is still present in the emitted assembly of its own function, for each (vendor x optimisation x mitigation) cell.
doesNotMeasure: IR-level or link-level checkpoints; this run observes exactly one checkpoint, 'asm'
scopeStatement.symmetryRule: Both vendors are observed with the SAME instrument (assembly of the target function). No clang result in this file is imported from the LLVM pass-plugin observer, because gcc has no counterpart and an asymmetric comparison would not be a comparison.

vendors.passPluginNote: gcc cannot load -fpass-plugin LLVM plugins. Pass-level attribution is UNSUPPORTED for this vendor by construction, not merely NOT_OBSERVED.

properties.note: Reference configuration is mitigation-ON: the defence only exists when the macro is defined. A mit-off LOST cell here is a configuration loss, not a compiler transformation.

multiMachine.reason: Exactly one host is available to this session. A second machine is an infrastructure requirement, not a measurement this generator declined to take. Nothing in the output may be read as evidence about machine-to-machine variation.

gccPassAttribution.reason: gcc does not load LLVM pass plugins, so the instrument that produces firstLossPass for clang has no gcc counterpart. Every gcc cell carries firstLossPass: null with this status. It must never be rendered as a pass name.

clangPassAttributionInThisRun.reason: This run deliberately uses the asm instrument for BOTH vendors so the comparison is symmetric. clang pass names exist elsewhere (_results/envelope.json) but are not imported here; importing them would silently change the instrument mid-table.
